findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: C is the only hedged option ('may have been written down'), and hedged caveats about record reliability are the key-shaped form for a 'what are we told about the counts' stem; D carries an absolutizer ('from the first season through to the last') and is implausible standing alone for a run of counts long enough to have a 1931 start on the table in A.

CROSS_QUESTION: q:3's stem presupposes that few dace enter the pass, which independently corroborates B's limb (netting below the weir out-catching the trap's dace record). Two options are therefore propped up by different channels, which splits rather than concentrates probability.
justification: I could narrow the field to three (D self-defeats against a multi-decade record) and I could see that C is the only hedged, reliability-flavoured option, which is the shape HP usually keys for a question about a book of counts. I could not decide between C's misidentification caveat and B's representativeness contrast, because q:3's stem quietly vouches for B's factual limb. Roughly 45% on C, so a real form channel that does not reach a single option reliably.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION: q:5 option D ('one fish gets up easily while two others mostly do not, and the different reason in each case') plus q:3's stem (which assigns the dace the ENTRY failure) forces the grayling into the ASCENT-failure slot, which is exactly q:2 option D's content. The phrase 'mostly do not' in q:5 D is a near-verbatim match for 'Most of those that entered the pass did not reach its top pool'.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: B is off the unit's axis (a tagging-sample fact rather than a passage-performance fact) and reads as filler, dropping the live field to three.

MIRRORED_TWIN: C ('their size, rather than their build') inverts the real fisheries fact that grayling fail passes on leaping ability, i.e. build, not size — but it is still a grayling-fails statement, so it soaks up part of the same inference and blunts the leak.
justification: I could infer with fair confidence that the grayling are one of the failing species and that their failure is an ascent failure, not an entry failure, purely by triangulating q:3's stem against q:5's option D. What I could not do is choose cleanly between the two grayling-fails options: D states the outcome, C states a mechanism, and the stem's neutral 'what are we told about' does not tell me which the item wants. About 50-55% on D — just under the kill line.

findings: ENTAILMENT: the stem's wording 'go INTO the pass' presupposes the failure is at the entrance, which excludes B outright (B explains failure BETWEEN pools, i.e. after entry). The stem hands back one of the four options for free.

CROSS_QUESTION: q:5 option D's 'the different reason in each case' plus q:2's ascent-failure slot for the grayling reinforces that the dace reason must NOT be the inter-pool drop — a second, independent route to eliminating B.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: A is the longest option and the only two-clause causal statement (route plus insufficient attraction flow); length-and-specificity is a live form cue here.
WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: failure of attraction flow at the entrance is the canonical explanation for a fish pass that fish will not enter — domain knowledge a Swedish 18-year-old is unlikely to hold.
justification: I could eliminate B on the stem's own wording alone, which is a genuine free gift, and the length/specificity of A plus the textbook status of the attraction-flow explanation pushed me onto A. I could not separate A from C (a timing mismatch) or D (shoaling behaviour) on anything other than form and outside knowledge — all three are entry explanations and all three are plausible. About 45-50% on A.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: the stem's 'What is IMPLIED' mildly disfavours B and D, which are both stated-purpose statements ('they were cut to…', 'they were meant to…') rather than inferences, concentrating roughly 0.5 on the two outcome-explanation options A and C.

MIRRORED_TWIN: D is B's overreach twin — B says the orifices take SOME water out of the notches, D says they were meant to REPLACE those notches. Replacing notches with orifices cut into the same walls is implausible standing alone, so D drops out and B survives as the sane member of the pair.

NOTE (batch20 calibration): A and C are NOT a contradictory dyad — an unusually heavy spate filling the lower orifice and height explaining why the upper stayed clear are mutually compatible, so this half of the set does not concentrate the way a true two-way dyad would.
justification: I could see that one orifice filled and one stayed clear (the option set gives that contrast away), and I could use the 'implied' register cue to push away from the two stated-purpose options. I could not choose between the river-side explanation (A, hedged with 'probably') and the position-side explanation (C, unhedged causal); I took C only because the stem asks about the orifices and C attributes the difference to a property of the orifices while A attributes it to the river. About 35% — barely above chance.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION: the four sibling stems are a table of contents. They name the trap's book of counts (q:1), the grayling (q:2), the dace and why so few enter (q:3), and the 2023 orifices (q:4). Option D — 'a pass that one fish gets up easily while two others mostly do not, and the different reason in each case' — is the only option that inventories exactly that: two named failing species, a per-species reason, and a pass to describe.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (odd-one-out): C introduces population DECLINE above the weir, a topic no stem or sibling option touches; A elevates water temperature, which appears nowhere but as a single distractor in q:2. Both are off the unit's demonstrated content and self-eliminate.

CROSS_QUESTION: q:3's stem explicitly supplies one of D's 'different reasons' (the dace entry problem), and q:2's option set supplies the other (the grayling ascent problem), so D is vouched for from two directions before the passage is opened.
justification: This is answerable without the passage. The last-position main-idea question is solved by reading the other four stems and matching their subject inventory against the four summaries; only D covers the ground the siblings demonstrably cover, and the two rival summaries import topics (decline, temperature) that the siblings never raise. About 65% on D. The channel is STUDENT-AVAILABLE — pure form and cross-question matching, no domain knowledge required.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION: gap (3)'s option set (clearance / giveaway / markdown / liquidation) fixes the passage's domain as retail selling and pricing. In that domain 'fetched' is the idiomatic price verb ('the lot fetched X'), which privileges D over three generic acquisition verbs.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (odd-one-out, weak): earned / gained / fetched are all obtain-verbs; 'returned' sits slightly apart as a yield verb. The separation is too soft to eliminate it outright.
justification: With no passage, the only thing I could use was the sibling gaps: gap (3) leaks the register of the whole text, and that register makes 'fetched' the collocationally right verb. I could not confirm the sentence frame, and 'earned' and 'gained' both survive in a commerce sentence, so this is about 35% — a real cross-gap channel at low strength.

findings: No channel found. The set is four inflections of one verb (keep / kept / keeping / to keep); nothing in the option set, the prompt, or the sibling gaps constrains which non-finite or finite form the missing frame demands.
NOTE: register, length, hedging, absolutizer and odd-one-out cues are all null here by construction — a single-lemma inflection set is informationally inert without the sentence.
justification: I could infer nothing at all. The pick of 'to keep' is a bare construction-frequency prior with no support from the item, and I would not bet above the 25% base rate on it. This is the one target in the batch that is genuinely inert stems-only.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (register): the set splits 2+2 on markedness. 'giveaway' is informal and semantically extreme (far below value) and 'liquidation' is an absolutizer (a business being wound up); 'clearance' and 'markdown' are the two neutral retail terms. A test-wise student drops the two marked extremes and is left with a coin flip, concentrating roughly 0.7 on two options — this is the 2+2 shape that the batch20 note identifies as a genuine channel, not an inert exclusivity cluster.
justification: I could halve the field on register alone, without any passage. I could not split 'clearance' from 'markdown' — one is the event, the other the price cut, and only the sentence frame decides. About 35% on A.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE: 'amply' and 'thinly' are contradictories on a single variable (quantity/density), a true two-way dyad that concentrates roughly 0.5 on those two, while 'briefly' (time) and 'openly' (concealment) sit on unrelated axes and read as filler.

CROSS_QUESTION (weak): the retail/selling-off register established by gap (3) and gap (1) tilts the dyad slightly toward the scarcity member ('thinly stocked', 'thinly attended') over the abundance member.
justification: I could see the antonym dyad immediately and drop the two off-axis adverbs, which is a real halving of the field. I could not break the dyad from inside the item; the tilt toward 'thinly' comes only from the commerce register the other gaps leak. About 35% on C.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (odd-one-out): 'Occasionally' is a frequency adverb, not a discourse connective like the other three, so it is a form-visible weak distractor and the live field is three, not four.

PAIR_STRUCTURE: 'Still' and 'Therefore' are contradictories on the direction-of-inference variable (contrast vs consequence). 'Granted' sits on the contrast side with 'Still', so the set is 2 contrast / 1 consequence / 1 off-class — a student who can tell the paragraph needs a contrast is down to a coin flip.
justification: I could eliminate one option on word-class alone and map the remaining three onto a contrast/consequence axis. I could not tell which direction the missing junction runs, nor split the two concessives, so my pick of 'Still' is barely above the raised 33% floor. About 30%.

findings: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: paper-conservation fact. Pressure-sensitive tape adhesive that has migrated into the sheet makes the paper translucent and greasy-looking — C is the standard, true observation. D asserts the opposite of the field's central difficulty (the brown stain in the fibres is precisely what solvent does NOT remove, which is why tape staining is notorious), so D is eliminable as the false clean-solution claim. A misattributes the brown to oxidised plasticiser, a conflation of the carrier film's embrittlement with the adhesive's degradation. B garbles the heat/solvent rule of thumb.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (student-available secondary cue): D is the only option that promises the problem fully solved ('once the solvent is matched… the brown comes out with it'), and in a text framed around a difficult conservation problem the clean-solution option is a standing distractor shape.
justification: I could answer this without the passage, but almost entirely on outside knowledge: three of the four options are recognisably wrong to anyone who has read about tape removal, leaving C as the only clean true statement. What I could not get from form alone is much of anything — the four options sit on four different axes (stain origin, technique selection, optical symptom, stain removal) and there is no dyad, no length cue and no hedging asymmetry. About 60% on C. CALIBRATION: this channel NEEDS DOMAIN KNOWLEDGE a Swedish 18-year-old almost certainly lacks; it is NOT student-available except for the weak clean-solution cue on D. Reportable, but low practical exposure for the intended cohort.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (register): the stem asks what can be CONCLUDED, which disfavours options that read as stated rules rather than derived patterns. C (an annual meeting settling which books to buy) is a governance rule and the only option not derivable from borrowing/payment records, so it self-eliminates; B (a penny a day past the fortnight) also reads as a stated tariff.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (odd-one-out): three options (A, B, D) are ledger-shaped inferences drawn from columns of a borrowing register; C alone is not, dropping the live field to three.
justification: I could use the stem's 'concluded' to push away from the rule-shaped options and I could tell that the evidence base is a borrowing ledger with named volumes ('the travels', 'the sermons'). I could not choose among the three ledger inferences — a same-day reissue (A), an overdue tariff (B) and a non-borrower lapse (D) are all equally derivable shapes. I took D because a correlation between not borrowing and dropping out is the most conclusion-flavoured of the three. About 35%.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (length/compound): C is the only two-part answer (an institutional decision AND a natural indicator) against three single-cause simplifications. The nuanced compound option is a strong key shape in HP LÄS and is visible without the text.
MIRRORED_TWIN: B reverses the causal arrow — herd-girls are hired BECAUSE the moving date is set, not the other way round — so it is implausible standing alone and drops out.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: the byastämma/byalag fixing the buföringsdag, moderated by how far the leafing had come, is the documented arrangement. Partly available to a Swedish student as general cultural knowledge, unlike the ELF domain cases.
justification: I could eliminate B on causal direction alone and I could see that C is the only option with the compound, nuanced shape HP tends to key. I could not rule out A (winter fodder running out) or D (snow and ice going), both of which are real and commonly-cited drivers of the same event, and either could be what this particular text says. About 55% on C — a real channel sitting just under the kill line.

findings: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: kulning — the herding call — was personal to each vallkulla and recognised by her own animals, while horn and lur signals carried conventional, fixed meanings. This is culturally well-known in Sweden, so the channel is at least partly STUDENT-AVAILABLE, not specialist.

MIRRORED_TWIN: A inverts a physical fact — a horn carries further through forest than a human voice, which is the entire reason for having one — so A is implausible standing alone and eliminates itself.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (odd-one-out on the abstraction axis): D is the only option that contrasts the two on a semiotic dimension (idiosyncratic vs codified); A, B and C all contrast on mundane physical, temporal or locational dimensions and read as filler variants of one another.
justification: This is answerable without the passage. The personal-call-versus-fixed-signal contrast is both the culturally correct fact and the only option operating on the dimension a text would bother to draw, and A actively self-destructs on acoustics. About 65% on D. CALIBRATION: mixed — the odd-one-out form cue is student-available on its own, and the kulning fact is common Swedish cultural knowledge rather than specialist domain knowledge.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION: q:1 option B embeds the clause 'lejda för sommaren', which is a direct contradictory of q:3 option D ('gällde ett tjänsteår och inte en enskild sommar'). The two cannot both be true, so a student who settles either question gains information about the other — a genuine cross-question link, though it runs between a distractor and an option rather than to a key.

NOTE: form cues CANCEL three ways here, which is why this stays a flag and not worse. A is the compound option, B carries the key-shaped hedge ('varierade något'), and D carries the key-shaped contrastive correction ('och inte'). Three options wear key-shaped clothing, so no single form cue survives.
justification: I could spot the contradiction between q:1's 'hired for the summer' and q:3's 'a service year, not a single summer', which is a real leak across the unit. I could not use it to land on a key, because the mutually cancelling form cues leave A, B and D within a few points of each other. I took A (spring agreement, payment largely in kind) as the most standard description of fäbod pay. About 33% — essentially chance, but the cross-question tie is worth reporting.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION: the three sibling stems form a table of contents — buföringen (q:1), vallkullornas rop och hornsignaler (q:2), fäbodfolkets lön (q:3). All three are about the herd-girls and their summer work, which is verbatim what option A names ('Vallkullorna och sommararbetet i skogen').

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (odd-one-out): C ('jordbruket och omvandlingen kring sekelskiftet') and D ('skogsbetet och de igenväxande markerna') both name land-use change, a topic no sibling stem or option touches anywhere in the unit; B ('avståndet och kravet på hållbarhet') is close to semantically incoherent as a title for any of this material and reads as pure filler.
justification: This is answerable without the passage and it is the cleanest leak in the batch. Reading the other three stems tells you the text is about the people of the fäbod and their summer work; only A says that, and the two land-use rivals are about something the unit demonstrably never discusses. About 70% on A. CALIBRATION: fully STUDENT-AVAILABLE — form and cross-question matching only, no domain knowledge needed.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION: q:2's entire option set presupposes a live proposal to move the market off the square to 'fältet'. That presupposition needs a reason, and D ('sexton av de sökande blev utan plats') is the only q:1 option that supplies one — the scarcity fact is the argumentative premise the sibling question is standing on.
MIRRORED_TWIN: C ('nya sökande brukar gå före de gamla') inverts the near-universal seniority rule in stall allocation and is implausible standing alone, so it drops out.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (weak): A and C are procedural rules, B and D are numeric facts, and the stem's 'stämmer med texten' is the detail-check shape that usually keys a number.
justification: I could eliminate C on plausibility and I could see from q:2's options that the text's argument needs a scarcity premise, which points at D. I could not rule out B ('fyra stånd tillkom inför förra hösten'), which is exactly the shape of a concession fact a debate piece would also carry, nor A. About 45-50% on D.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (hedging/moderation): D is the conditional, trial-and-evaluate option, and the measured position is a persistent key shape for 'vilken hållning ger textförfattaren uttryck för' in a debate item.
CROSS_QUESTION: q:1's option set frames the square as oversubscribed, corroborating the pro-relocation direction and arguing against C, the status-quo option.

NOTE (batch20 calibration): the 3+1 shape — A, B and D all share the 'flytta till fältet' limb against C's 'stanna' — gives away the author's DIRECTION but is informationally INERT for picking, because the three move-options are pairwise incompatible on their riders and each still sits at the base rate. I am explicitly not scoring the 3+1 as a concentrating dyad.
justification: I could establish, without the passage, that the author is very probably pro-relocation — three of four options carry that limb and q:1 supplies the scarcity premise. What I could not do is pick the rider: endure the bad years (A), one day only (B), or a one-year trial (D) are three genuinely different positions and only the passage settles which. I took D on the moderation cue alone. About 40%.

findings: RULE 15 (a) ONE-WAY LEAK — NOT FOUND at strength. No option in either question carries a concessive or presuppositional clause that asserts the fact the other question tests. q:2's options presuppose only that a relocation proposal exists and that the market currently runs more than one day (from B's 'men hållas en dag'); neither of those is what q:1 tests, which is how the square's places were allocated and how many applicants missed out. q:2 option C's 'torghandlarnas flertal' presupposes the traders were polled, which again does not touch q:1's allocation facts. Running it the other way, no q:1 option asserts anything about the author's stance: q:1 D supplies a premise that RATIONALISES relocation but does not entail it, since an author could cite the same sixteen shut-out applicants to demand MORE stalls on the square and thereby support q:2 C.

RULE 15 (b) SYMMETRIC VOUCHING — FOUND, mild-to-moderate. Both option sets are drawn from one small factual world: a single square, a fixed stock of stalls, a pool of applicants, a proposed alternative site, a body of torghandlare with a majority view, and a market of more than one day's length. Reading the six options together reconstructs a usable situation model without the passage — a crowded square, more applicants than places, a multi-day market, a relocation proposal, divided traders. Within that model the members corroborate each other asymmetrically: q:1 D is the only q:1 fact the q:2 world actually NEEDS, and the q:2 move-cluster is the only stance the q:1 world actually motivates.

JOINT SOLVABILITY: partial. A test-wise student working both questions together gets q:1 to roughly 45-50% on D and gets q:2's DIRECTION to roughly 0.8 pro-relocation, but cannot convert the direction into a single option because the three move-options differ only on riders that the passage alone resolves. Net effect: about one of the two questions is materially compromised, not both.

ODDS TRANSFER: yes, and it runs both ways on one shared variable (scarcity). Committing to q:1 D pushes q:2 away from C and into the move-cluster; committing to q:2 C (status quo, traders are right) pushes q:1 away from D and toward B ('fyra stånd tillkom inför förra hösten'), the square-is-coping fact. The questions are therefore not independent.
justification: As a pair this unit leaks its situation rather than its answers. I could reconstruct the whole dispute from the option sets alone and I could fix the author's direction with fair confidence, but the item's discrimination sits on riders that no cross-question channel reaches. No hard entailment leak in either direction; the exposure is symmetric vouching through a shared small world. The pair pick 'D' is the joint reading — q:1 D and q:2 D — with q:1 the stronger of the two limbs.

findings: ENTAILMENT: the stem's own noun does the work. 'Finrummet' lexically presupposes a room kept for the finest occasions and the most honoured callers, and option D ('de gäster som huset höll allra högst') does little more than restate that presupposition in other words. The stem entails the option.

PAIR_STRUCTURE: A and D are contradictories on the guest-status variable — the utilitarian errand-caller against the most honoured guest — concentrating roughly 0.5 on that dyad, with B (longest journey) and C (announced in advance) sitting on unrelated axes. The stem's own lexeme then breaks the dyad decisively toward D.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: the finrum/kök division, with everyday and errand callers kept to the kitchen and formal guests shown into the parlour, is ordinary Swedish domestic knowledge — fully STUDENT-AVAILABLE, not specialist.

CROSS_QUESTION: two of q:2's four options carry presuppositional clauses that independently characterise the room as ceremonial and sparingly used — A presupposes the house once held its funerals there, D presupposes the room was formerly unheated. Both point q:1 at D, and crucially the leak does not depend on resolving which of them is q:2's key.
justification: This is answerable without the passage and by the intended cohort. The stem hands over its own answer: a question asking who was received in the FIN-room, offered an option saying 'the guests the house held highest', is close to self-answering, and the contradictory pair structure with A makes the choice a two-horse race that the lexeme then settles. The sibling question's options reinforce it from a second direction. About 70% on D. The only thing that could rescue it is a counterintuitive twist in the passage, which the neutral 'enligt texten' phrasing gives no sign of. CALIBRATION: STUDENT-AVAILABLE, form and lexical only.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (inference shape): the stem asks for a slutsats, and D's claim is a physical precondition ('kunde ställas dit först sedan elementen fanns') which is logically tight, whereas A's is a bare temporal correlation ('fick sin plats sedan begravningarna flyttat'), which is the post-hoc shape HP habitually uses as a distractor. That asymmetry is the only real cue in the set.

NOTE (batch20 calibration): A and D are CO-AXIAL, not contradictory — 'a prior ceremonial constraint lifted' and 'a prior thermal constraint lifted' can both be true at once — so this half of the set does NOT concentrate probability the way a genuine two-way dyad would, and I am not scoring it as one.

CROSS_QUESTION (weak, reverse direction): q:1's answer characterises the finrum as a status room, which argues mildly against C (the set finally moving out to the kitchen) but leaves A, B and D untouched.
justification: I could tell that the unit's small world contains a cold ceremonial parlour, home funerals, a kitchen and one television set, and I could use the 'slutsats' framing to prefer a tight precondition over a loose sequence. I could not get further: A, C and D are each a real and well-attested Swedish social-history trope and any of the three would make a satisfying conclusion. About 33-35% on D — near chance, reported as a flag only because the inference-shape cue is genuine.

findings: RULE 15 (a) ONE-WAY LEAK — FOUND, and it is the strong form. q:2 option A carries the presuppositional clause 'sedan begravningarna flyttat till kapellet', which presupposes the house formerly held its funerals in that room; q:2 option D carries 'först sedan elementen fanns', which presupposes the room was formerly unheated. Each clause asserts a fact about what kind of room the finrum was — ceremonial, sparingly used, fired only for occasions — and that is precisely the variable q:1 tests. The leak therefore lands on q:1's answer: a room that hosted funerals and stood cold is a room for the most honoured guests (q:1 D), not for errand-callers (q:1 A). Critically, the leak is ROBUST TO NON-RESOLUTION: the student does not need to know which of q:2 A or D is correct, because the presupposition survives in both, so merely reading q:2's options settles the character of the room. The leak is one-way: q:2 → q:1.

RULE 15 (b) SYMMETRIC VOUCHING — FOUND, strong. Both option sets are drawn from one very small factual world — a single room in a single house, its guests, its furniture, its heating, its funerals, the kitchen next door, and one television set. Every one of the six options is a fact about that room, so reading them together reconstructs the room's entire biography with no passage at all: formal reception room, cold, once used for funerals, later home to a television, with the kitchen as the everyday alternative. The sets corroborate each other coherently in one combination and incoherently in the other — q:1 D with q:2 A/D gives a consistent 'status room, sparingly used, later repurposed' model, while q:1 A (errand-callers) with q:2 C (evenings displaced to the kitchen) gives an incoherent everyday-room model, since a room already used for errands would not need its evenings displaced.

JOINT SOLVABILITY: high for q:1, low for q:2. Worked as a pair, q:1 goes to roughly 0.70 on D — the stem's own lexeme plus the pair leak plus the contradictory A/D dyad — while q:2 stays near 0.33 because its three live options are co-axial and the transfer in that direction is marginal.

ODDS TRANSFER: strongly asymmetric. Answering q:2 (or merely reading its options) materially shifts q:1; answering q:1 shifts q:2 only from four live options to three, arguing mildly against C and leaving the A/D split untouched.
justification: The pair fails. q:2's option set functions as a gloss on the finrum for anyone who has not read the passage, and it hands q:1 its answer through presuppositions that hold whichever way q:2 itself resolves. This is the textbook one-way leak the rule is written to catch, compounded by a very small shared factual world that lets the two option sets vouch for each other. The pair pick 'D' is the joint reading — q:1 D at high confidence, q:2 D at low. CALIBRATION: STUDENT-AVAILABLE in full; the channel needs nothing beyond knowing what a finrum is, which every Swedish 18-year-old does.
